stage1.impression: A strong, simple idea: a lone amber speaker in a rain-swept black lava flat at dusk, mirrored in a puddle that leads the eye straight to it, with room for type in the sky. It still reads as CG: the rain streaks are uniform and in the mid-field read as pins standing on the ground, the sky is soft and beige-pink rather than a storm, a pale far-field strip makes a hard seam under the horizon, and the cabinet is a dark, uniform amber block silhouetted against the bright band with no light passing through its acrylic.

blocking_9: The cabinet reads as lit, glowing amber acrylic: front face lum_median 90-135 in [580,360,690,395] with a visible transmitted rim on the sun side, not a dark block at about the ground's value (now 52 vs ground 38-47)
The cabinet's colour reads golden, not brown: blue channel not fully crushed (now b_median 0 over the whole cabinet) and delta-E2000 against a golden amber under 25 (now 47.6 vs #D9A520)
The sky reads as a sulphurous yellow-green storm, not a beige-pink overcast: upper sky b_median well under r/g (now r177 g171 b141)
No pale band or seam where the near ground meets the far field (now a step from lum 113 at y 425-448 to 48 at y 450-470)
Rain in the mid-field does not read as sticks planted on the rock; streaks fade into the ground band rather than standing on it
Splash crowns read as water, not as bright bokeh sprites dotted evenly across the puddle
Sky resolution holds at full size (no smeared, upscaled cloud texture)

defects.what: Cabinet is dark and uniform (lum_median 43, r63 g41 b0): amber reads brown, silhouetted against the sky, no light passes through the acrylic, blue fully crushed
Horn reads as a liquid-chrome mirror with a dark smear inside (lum p5 6, p95 223), more like polished metal than tinted resin
Pale grey far-field strip (lum 113) with a hard edge onto the dark near ground (lum 48): a seam at the horizon
Left ridge reads as a flat green cut-out, greener than anything else in the frame
Rain streaks against dark ground read as vertical pins standing on the rock, evenly spaced and equal in length
Sky is soft/upscaled and beige-pink (b_median 141), not a storm and not sulphurous; rain over it reads as uniform scratches
Splash crowns are bright dots evenly scattered, reading as sprites or bokeh rather than crowns and ripples
Contact line under the cabinet is a dark band (lum 25) with little water meniscus; the cabinet reads placed on, not standing in, the water
Reflection is dark and muddy (lum_median 37), less a mirror than a brown smear

changes.problem: The cabinet is underlit and reads as a dark brown block silhouetted against the bright horizon instead of glowing amber acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 52.7, r76 g51 b0; whole cabinet [500,345,700,605] lum_median 42.7 against ground 38-47 and sky band 217

change.to: irradiance 2.2, #F1E6B8, moved to 40 deg camera-left so it fills the front face

changes.expected: Front face lifts to a mid-tone gold that separates from the ground and the sky band; the white lining starts to read through the acrylic.

changes.problem: No light visibly passes through the tinted acrylic; the sun-side edge has no glow, so the material's point (tinted, translucent) is lost.

evidence.measured: right edge step 42.5 over 10 px but the edge itself stays dark amber; cabinet b_median 0 throughout

change.setting: Lamps: 1 m card behind and right toward the sun
change.to: 2.0, 1.5 m, raised to the cabinet's mid-height so it shines through the right side panel

changes.expected: A bright amber transmitted rim on the right side and a warm glow through the side panel; the amber spills into the puddle under the right edge.

changes.problem: The sky and haze read as a beige-pink overcast, not the sulphurous yellow-green storm the frame is about.

evidence.measured: r177 g171 b141; horizon band [900,300,1200,420] r243 g231 b206, warm-neutral

change.to: 0.0018 /m, #BFC85A (and grade the sky HDRI alone toward yellow-green: -15 blue in its highlights, not the global white balance, so the speaker's colour holds)

changes.expected: Sky and far field take a sulphurous yellow-green cast with depth; blue drops well below red and green in the upper sky.

changes.problem: A pale far-field strip meets the dark near ground in a hard line under the horizon, a modelled-ground seam.

evidence.measured: lum_median 113 at y 425-448 against 48 at y 450-470; edge step -13 over 45-51 px in a 1-D profile but a visible line in the crop

change.setting: Ground: far-field film roughness and the near/far transition
change.from: film roughness 0.08, far field flat to the horizon
change.to: film roughness 0.18 with the near rock texture blended into the far field over 15-40 m (no single boundary), and the haze of c3 on top

changes.expected: The ground darkens and brightens gradually into the horizon with no line; the strip at y 425-448 drops toward the near ground's value.

changes.problem: Mid-field rain streaks stand out bright against the dark rock and read as pins planted in the ground, all the same length and spacing.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 60 over median 38: streaks at about 1.6x the ground, vertical, evenly spaced (seen in crop)

change.from: opacity 0.12 to 0.5, none ending within 10 cm of the ground
change.to: opacity 0.06 to 0.3, density halved below 1.5 m height so streaks thin out toward the rock, none ending within 60 cm of the ground; lean spread 3 -> 6 deg

changes.expected: Rain reads against the sky and the bright band, not as sticks on the ground; the ground band is quieter.

changes.problem: Splash crowns read as bright evenly scattered dots, not water.

evidence.measured: point highlights scattered evenly across the puddle and the reflection (seen at 2x crop)

change.from: 3 to 14 mm, opacity 0.2, even over the puddle chain
change.to: 450 crowns, opacity 0.12, clustered (density varied 4:1 in 1 m patches), each paired with a ripple ring of the 3 cm layer

changes.expected: Fewer, softer splashes that sit inside rings; the puddle reads as rained-on water rather than glitter.

changes.problem: The cabinet's base sits on a dark band with no meniscus or wet contact, so it reads placed on the water rather than standing in it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 25, p95 50: a dark band with no bright water line at the base

change.to: 4 cm deep, with a 5 mm meniscus fillet and a darker wet ring 10 cm around the base

changes.expected: A thin bright water line where the reflection meets the base; the cabinet reads as standing in the puddle with weight.

changes.problem: The left ridge reads as a flat green cut-out, greener than anything else in the frame, and pulls the eye left.

evidence.measured: a saturated green silhouette with a hard top against the pale band (seen in 2x crop)

change.setting: Rocks: low broken ridge at 200 m
change.to: darkened 40 % and desaturated to the rock colour, lost further into the c3 haze

changes.expected: The ridge sits back as a faint grey-olive form; nothing green on the horizon competes with the speaker.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn read as tinted resin rather than a liquid-chrome mirror (its reflection is a dark smear with p95 223)
out_of_scope.why: That is the horn's material, part of the speaker; a fill card into the throat may help, but the finish itself is fixed.

out_of_scope.request: Lighter golden tone in the acrylic itself (cabinet blue channel is 0 throughout, delta-E 47.6 to #D9A520)
out_of_scope.why: The tint is the speaker's colour; c1 and c2 relight it, but if it still reads brown under even light the material's tint or density needs checking by the owner.
